title: On‑demand reserve lanes and amortized overage billing for short bursts
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated occasionally need short-lived increases in throughput (30s–30m) to absorb traffic spikes. Current surge pool behavior can either be too conservative (rejecting traffic) or too aggressive (charging immediate overage at full rate), and operators lack fine-grained controls to define which requests may preempt reserved capacity.

Proposal: Implement 'reserve lanes' — a lightweight, per-customer, preauthorized borrowing mechanism that draws transient tokens from a shared surge reservoir. Reserve lanes provide guaranteed short-window throughput with a leaky‑bucket amortization of billing: rather than charging immediate full overage rates, we amortize the cost across a configurable smoothing window (e.g., 1–24 hours) and surface a clear amortized overage charge. Integrate reserve lanes with autoscaling policies and fleet controls so that: (1) autoscaler can use reserve lanes before spinning new capacity, (2) reserve lanes respect preemption windows for higher‑priority tenants, (3) Console exposes controls and projected amortized cost.

Goals: reduce failed requests during real customer spikes, lower operational churn by avoiding unnecessary capacity provisioning, and provide predictable billing signals for short bursts.

Scope: runtime changes (token accounting, queue-weighted allocation, preemption), billing pipeline changes (amortization engine and invoice line item), Console UX for reserve lane settings and amortized cost preview, and API/SDK additions to annotate requests with burst_priority and reserve_lane_hint.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime: requests annotated with reserve_lane_hint can consume transient tokens up to a per-customer ceiling and are rate-limited by a leaky-bucket that refills from the global surge reservoir.
Autoscaler: policy option 'prefer_reserve_lane' routes burst traffic to reserve lanes before scaling; documented behavior for cooldowns and minimum spin-up thresholds.

Preemption: owner-configurable preemption tiers ensure that higher-tier customers can reclaim in-flight reserve tokens with a transparent fallback path and <500ms error surface when reclaiming occurs.

Billing: amortization engine records transient token usage and emits an amortized overage line on invoices that matches the smoothing window; audit logs contain both raw usage and amortized charge calculations.
Console: new Dedicated > Capacity > Reserve Lanes panel to set per-customer ceiling, smoothing window, and view 24h projected amortized cost granularity down to 5m.
API: new fields in capacity allocation API to configure reserve_lane ceilings and burst_priority; SDK updated with example usage and integration tests.
Observability: dashboards show reserve token pool health, per-customer borrow history, amortized-charge vs raw-charge drift, and SLO impact charts for 99/95 token latency.
End-to-end tests: integration test that simulates 10x baseline traffic spike for 15m and validates no more than 1% request errors and invoice reflects amortized charge within 2% of model expectation.
comments: 2026-03-02 Marco Chen: Initial design posted to Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Reserve+Lanes+Design) — looking for feedback from billing and runtime teams on amortization model.

2026-03-03 Priya Nanduri (Billing): Recommended amortization minimum window of 1 hour to avoid noise in invoices; flagged tax/regulatory implications for EMEA customers — added as dependency for finance review.

2026-03-04 Jonah Reyes (Runtime): Prototype token allocator implemented in branch github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3421 — basic leaky-bucket accounting and demo harness included. Observed contention when >30% of nodes consumed surge tokens concurrently; need backpressure strategy.

2026-03-06 Aisha Patel: Design review meeting notes — decided to weight allocations by queue_priority to avoid starving latency-sensitive customer queues. Agreed on preemption window of 10s for soft reclaim and 500ms for hard reclaim with explicit fallback HTTP header (X-Reserve-Reclaimed).

2026-03-08 Marco Chen: Billing pipeline spike aggregation sketch uploaded (https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1ReserveBillingSketch) — plan to implement amortization as a post-processor that reads token usage stream and writes amortized entries to billing DB.

2026-03-09 SRE: Load test scheduled for 2026-03-15 to validate inter-region surge reservoirs and cross-region draining behavior. Added a follow-up ticket to observe tail latencies during reservoir drain (ENG-14067).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: amortization smooths billing but increases short-term revenue deferral; we chose amortization window configurability per account to let finance balance predictability vs. cash flow. Need legal review for EMEA invoicing rules. Runtime must ensure reserve lanes cannot be used to subvert tenant isolation — token accounting validated with strict per-customer quotas and audit logging.
